text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared repository. Every time code is added, automated builds start immediately, so the software is always checked and ready to use. As part of the build, the system runs tests to make sure everything works correctly. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear sequence, from building the code to running tests and reporting results. By using CI pipelines, teams can find and fix bugs faster, work together more easily, and release better software with less risk.
